title: Map a list to uppercase
description:
Write a function `map_upper(strings)` that returns a new list with every string in `strings` uppercased, using `map()`.

Covers source items 1 and 3 (uppercase the countries list, then the names list) as one exercise - map() applied to either list works the same way.
hints: Function to consider: map(), with str.upper as the callback

map(str.upper, strings) applies .upper() to every item in strings without a for loop - str.upper used this way (not called as name.upper()) is the function itself, ready to be applied to each item map() hands it.
Return list(map(str.upper, strings)) - map() alone produces a lazy iterator, so wrap it in list() to get a real list back.
expected_behavior: Returns every string uppercased, in the original order.
explanation: str.upper passed by name (not called) is a function that map() can apply to every item - it's the same underlying method as text.upper(), just referenced rather than invoked directly.
